source_review.notes: Checked current ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 and 15288:2023 metadata; NASA requirement-writing and verification/validation appendix guidance; SEBoK 2.14 System Requirements Definition and System Verification; INCOSE Guide for Writing Requirements version 4 metadata; and the Mavin et al. EARS DOI. NASA and SEBoK returned HTTP 200, and the DOI resolver returned HTTP 202. ISO and INCOSE returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client; their current metadata/content was independently inspected during authoring, but command-line reachability is not claimed.

evidence: Reviewed the requirement and verification-evidence tuples, acceptance equivalence, four distinct verification/validation relations, acceptance predicate and evidence scope, individual quality conjunction, set-quality conjunction, and five invariants.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every symbol is introduced before use. Requirement verification, requirement validation, product verification, system validation, acceptance, and certification remain distinct.

evidence: Executed requirement-quality-record-check under Python 3.14.4 and independently recomputed five records, one well-formed declared record, missing source RQ-004, missing oracle RQ-003, missing conditions and vague signal RQ-002:quickly, compound signal RQ-005:and, and wrong modal RQ-004:should.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The checker is exact for declared fields and bounded lexical signals only; it cannot establish semantic clarity, necessity, atomicity, feasibility, source fidelity, set completeness, or oracle validity.

evidence: Re-derived the separation among requirements artifact verification, source-intent validation, realization verification, and outcome validation and confirmed no relation implies all others without additional evidence.
Checked the discrimination relation between observed evidence and a predeclared acceptance predicate and the scope restriction on any pass conclusion.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The quality conjunctions are review predicates, not decidable completeness theorems or universal guarantees.

evidence: Reviewed vague/absolute language, pronouns, logical and temporal scope, inclusive bounds, strong safety prohibitions, low-sample quantiles, invalid/duplicate/concurrent input, failure/recovery, test article pedigree, model assumptions, missing/censored observations, wrong-level evidence, human judgment, clinical AI, spacecraft safe mode, and physical emergency shutdown.

Challenged all ten examples and five answers for easy-test bias, tool-driven rewriting, inspection of settings instead of behavior, self-referential oracles, set-level gaps, proof overclaiming, and unsupported external authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-consequence acceptance remains conditional on applicable independence, domain competence, and safety, security, clinical, regulatory, or other external authority.

evidence: Traced meaning, source, discrimination, evidence-scope, and requirement-set invariants through exposition, ten worked examples, and five complete answers.

Verified that each verification construction names or explicitly requests configuration, conditions, stimulus, observations, oracle, calculation, tolerance/uncertainty, coverage, artifacts, and authority.
invariant_checking.notes: Individual textual quality never substitutes for source/operational coverage, relational consistency, combined feasibility, or verification closure.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents conditional relations and audit predicates but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed uses of verify, validate, prove, guarantee, evidence, complete, correct, feasible, atomic, testable, safe, secure, fair, clinical, and compliant.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-016/report.json records exact local execution evidence for declared fields and lexical signals.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes record-shape and lexical observations only. It cannot establish semantic requirement quality, test adequacy, source correctness, set completeness, system safety, clinical validity, fairness, conformity, or external review.

conceptual_review.notes: Professor-style review checked requirement quality, verification, validation, product/system verification, acceptance, certification, verifiability, testability, oracle, atomicity, completeness, feasibility, ambiguity, verification method, evidence scope, and success criterion for conceptual consistency.

practitioner_review.notes: Practitioner-style review checked service recovery, access control, latency, safety guards, maintainability, retention, routing algorithms, state conflicts, AI fairness, emergency shutdown, payment recovery, evacuation data, spacecraft safe mode, and medication-allergy warnings. Each example exposes assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limitations, and bounded conclusions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Pedagogical review confirmed progression from review scope and verification/validation distinctions through necessity, ambiguity classes, expression completeness, singularity, feasibility, discrimination, method/oracle, configuration, coverage, uncertainty, set review, findings, and bounded automation. Ten examples and five complete answers require critique, rewriting, evidence design, method comparison, and high-consequence review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
